title: 2015 HMMT November General Problem 10
statement: Let \(N\) be the number of functions \(f\) from \(\{1,2, \ldots, 101\} \rightarrow\{1,2, \ldots, 101\}\) such that \(f^{101}(1)=2\). Find the remainder when \(N\) is divided by 103.

solutions.text:
Answer: 43
For convenience, let \(n=101\). Compute the number of functions such that \(f^{n}(1)=1\). Since \(n\) is a prime, there are 2 cases: the order of 1 is either 1 or \(n\). The first case gives \(n^{n-1}\) functions, and the second case gives \((n-1)\) ! functions. By symmetry, the number of ways for \(f^{n}(1)=2\) is

\[\frac{1}{n-1} \cdot\left(n^{n}-n^{n-1}-(n-1)!\right)=n^{n-1}-(n-2)!\]

Plugging in \(n=101\), we need to find

\[\begin{gathered}
101^{100}-99!\equiv(-2)^{-2}-\frac{101!}{6} \\
=1 / 4-1 / 6=1 / 12=43 \quad(\bmod 103) .
\end{gathered}\]
